Title: Shelf-Life-Aware Production Planner
Description: Forecast weekly demand for perishable SKUs, then optimise production quantities, sequencing and safety stock (MIP) under line capacity, allergen changeover rules, shelf-life limits and demand uncertainty; quantify the improvement over a fair naive baseline in expired waste, stockouts and changeover hours.

Title: Domain brief and KPI specification
Description: As a operations analyst, I want a short domain brief and exact KPI definitions, so that every model assumption is defensible to a plant or quality manager.

Title: Reproducible environment
Description: As a solo builder, I want a scaffolded repo and a proven solver/forecasting toolchain on Windows, so that later work is not blocked by setup surprises.

Title: Weekly demand panel
Description: As a demand planner, I want a clean weekly demand panel for 12 perishable SKUs from real retail data, so that forecasts reflect real seasonality, noise and intermittency.

Title: Documented synthetic plant
Description: As a plant planner, I want a documented plant (line, rates, shelf lives, allergens, changeovers, costs), so that the optimiser solves a realistic, citable constrained problem.

Title: Forecast evaluation harness
Description: As a demand planner, I want a leak-free rolling-origin backtest with standard metrics, so that model comparisons are trustworthy.

Title: Statistical forecasting models
Description: As a demand planner, I want ARIMA/ETS and Prophet compared against naive benchmarks, so that I can justify which forecast feeds the planner.

Title: Forecast uncertainty
Description: As a supply chain analyst, I want calibrated forecast-error distributions and demand scenarios, so that safety stock and stress tests reflect real forecast error.

Title: Simulator and naive baseline
Description: As a operations analyst, I want a trusted plant simulator and a defensible baseline plan, so that improvements are measured against a fair comparator, not a strawman.

Title: Core MIP with allergen sequencing
Description: As a production planner, I want an optimiser that sizes and sequences runs under capacity, shelf life and allergen rules, so that plans cut waste and changeover time without violating food-safety rules.

Title: Service level, rolling horizon and independent checking
Description: As a production planner, I want safety-stock logic, weekly re-planning and an independent plan checker, so that plans are realistic, re-plannable and provably feasible.

Title: Quantified comparison vs baseline
Description: As a plant manager reviewing results, I want paired, statistically sound KPI comparisons with confidence intervals, so that I can trust the claimed improvement.

Title: Sensitivity and trade-off analysis
Description: As a plant manager reviewing results, I want to see where the advantage holds, shrinks or vanishes, so that I understand the limits of the result.

Title: Core dashboard
Description: As a non-technical reviewer, I want a dashboard showing KPIs, forecasts and weekly plans, so that I can grasp the result in two minutes without reading code.

Title: Explorer and run guide
Description: As a non-technical reviewer, I want to explore scenarios and launch the app easily, so that I can test my own what-ifs.

Title: Project documentation
Description: As a hiring manager or interviewer, I want a README, assumptions register and limitations section, so that I can judge rigor and reproduce the work.

Title: Portfolio packaging and QA
Description: As a the builder, I want resume bullets, pitch and a clean-clone reproducibility check, so that the project is interview-ready and every claim traces to an artifact.

Title: Spike: verify public data sources and access
Description: TIME BOX 1.5h. Confirm that the candidate public datasets exist, can be downloaded by a free account, and what their terms are. Candidates: Corporacion Favorita Grocery Sales Forecasting (Kaggle; train.csv, items.csv with `perishable` flag), M5 Forecasting (Walmart, Kaggle; FOODS department) as fallback, USDA FSIS FoodKeeper (CC0 JSON on data.gov) for shelf-life anchors. Actually open the files; do not rely on descriptions.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] docs/research/data_sources.md has a table: dataset, URL, licence/terms, access method, files, date range, row counts - each confirmed by opening the file
- [ ] Favorita items.csv confirmed to contain item_nbr, family, class, perishable; train.csv date range recorded
- [ ] FoodKeeper JSON downloaded and the fields used for shelf life (product name, min/max, metric) listed
- [ ] docs/decisions/ADR-001-data-source.md records primary source and fallback (M5 FOODS, or fully synthetic demand calibrated to published retail patterns) and the trigger for fallback
- [ ] If Kaggle access fails inside the time box the fallback is invoked and recorded; spike is closed either way

Title: Write domain brief and KPI definitions
Description: Write a <=4-page brief the builder can defend in an interview. Cover: FDA major food allergens (9, incl. sesame since 1 Jan 2023 under the FASTER Act); FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food (21 CFR Part 117) allergen cross-contact controls and sanitation; why allergen changeovers need cleaning (residue of allergen X must not reach a product not declaring X) and typical verification (swab/ATP/allergen test kits); shelf-life vocabulary (date of manufacture, best-by/use-by, FEFO vs FIFO, customer minimum remaining shelf life at receipt); lot sizing, changeovers, safety stock; OEE context (this project does not model OEE losses explicitly - say so). Then write the KPI spec.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] docs/research/domain_brief.md exists, <=4 pages, each factual claim has a citation link or is tagged UNVERIFIED
- [ ] docs/research/kpi_definitions.md defines, with formula, unit and denominator: expired waste (cases and % of produced), fill rate, lost cases, stockout-SKU-weeks, changeover hours, line utilisation, weeks of cover, WAPE, bias, MASE
- [ ] Each KPI lists the future code function name (placeholder) and the results column it will populate
- [ ] A glossary of >=15 terms is included (e.g. FEFO, cross-contact, CIP/wet clean, MSL, WAPE, lot sizing)
- [ ] A list of 'things I am unsure about' is included and copied to docs/assumptions.md as OPEN items

Title: Build weekly demand panel for 12 perishable SKUs
Description: Implement scripts/download_data.py (Kaggle API, or printed manual instructions) and src/shelflife/data/favorita.py. Select 12 SKUs with perishable=1 across 4-5 families (e.g. DAIRY, DELI, PREPARED FOODS, BREAD/BAKERY, EGGS) using a written rule (e.g. top volume among items non-zero in >=95% of weeks). Aggregate daily to weekly (Mon-Sun) and across all stores (a DC-level proxy). Handle: missing calendar days (e.g. 25 Dec absent in the source), negative sales (returns: clip to 0 and log count), fractional units (weighed items), partial first/last weeks (drop). Do not commit raw data. Include a short EDA notebook.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] data/processed/demand_weekly.parquet has columns sku_id, item_nbr, family, week_start, units; exactly 12 SKUs; no NaN; contiguous weeks per SKU; >=200 weeks per SKU
- [ ] SKU selection rule is written in the notebook and reproduced by code; selected item_nbr list saved to configs/skus.yaml
- [ ] pytest checks: schema, contiguity, non-negativity; rebuild is deterministic (file hash equal on two runs)
- [ ] notebooks/01_demand_eda.ipynb shows per-SKU time plot, seasonality (week-of-year) and CV / zero-share table
- [ ] `git status` shows no raw data committed; docs/assumptions.md records the 'retail sales as DC demand proxy' assumption

Title: Define synthetic plant parameters with sources
Description: Create configs/plant.yaml for a hypothetical refrigerated prepared-foods plant: one filling/packing line (the single bottleneck), weekly buckets. For each of 12 SKUs: family, allergen set (subset of the Big 9, assigned by family with rationale), shelf life at manufacture (days; anchored to USDA FoodKeeper ranges for comparable products where one exists, otherwise flagged ASSUMPTION), line rate (cases/h), minimum and maximum run size, unit cost. Line: weekly available hours (e.g. 2 shifts x 5 days x 8h less planned sanitation/maintenance), minimum remaining shelf life at shipment (%). Every parameter carries a `source:` field = citation URL | 'assumption' + plausible range.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] configs/plant.yaml loads through a pydantic (or dataclass) schema in src/shelflife/plant/config.py with validation errors on missing source
- [ ] Every parameter has a non-empty source; count of 'assumption' parameters is printed by `python -m shelflife.plant.config --report`
- [ ] Allergen sets only use the 9 FDA major allergens (validated in code)
- [ ] Shelf lives are 14-56 days for all SKUs (weekly-bucket model is invalid outside this; documented)
- [ ] docs/assumptions.md created with one row per assumption: ID, value, range, source, sensitivity-tested (Y/N, link)

Title: Allergen changeover matrix and capacity calibration
Description: Implement src/shelflife/plant/changeover.py. Rule: changeover i->j = base time (label/format) + allergen clean time if SKU i carries any allergen NOT declared on SKU j (residue would be an undeclared allergen); smaller clean/flavour-change time otherwise; allergen-free to anything is cheap. Times come from config ranges (assumptions; no public per-line dataset exists - flag it). Also calibrate a demand scale factor so that the baseline-style weekly load (production hours + changeovers) averages ~85% of available hours (a TARGET calibration assumption) and save to configs/calibration.yaml.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] pytest: for 10 hand-written SKU pairs, the matrix matches the expected clean/no-clean decision (incl. subset case: i={milk}, j={milk,soy} needs no allergen clean; i={milk,soy}, j={milk} does)
- [ ] Matrix is asymmetric where the rule says it should be; diagonal is 0
- [ ] docs/figures/changeover_heatmap.png exists
- [ ] configs/calibration.yaml contains scale_factor and the achieved mean utilisation (printed by scripts/calibrate.py)
- [ ] Changeover time ranges are listed in docs/assumptions.md as ASSUMPTION with low/base/high values

Title: Rolling-origin backtest harness and naive benchmarks
Description: src/shelflife/forecast/backtest.py. Windows: train >=104 weeks; VALIDATION year (52 weekly origins) used for model selection and error calibration; TEST year (final 52 weeks) used only for reporting. Expanding window, horizons 1-13. Metrics: WAPE, bias (signed % error), MASE. Benchmarks: naive, seasonal naive (52w), 4-week moving average. Standard output schema: sku_id, origin, horizon, target_week, y, yhat, model, window.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Output parquet follows the schema above for each benchmark model
- [ ] pytest leakage test: for every row, all training data < origin <= target_week
- [ ] results/forecast/benchmark_metrics.csv has WAPE/bias/MASE per SKU and aggregate for validation and test windows
- [ ] Window boundaries (dates) are written to configs/windows.yaml and asserted in tests
- [ ] Re-running with the same inputs gives identical metrics

Title: Forecast-error sigma table and demand-scenario generator
Description: From VALIDATION-year residuals of the selected models, build per-SKU, per-horizon error standard deviations (results/forecast/error_sigma.csv) used for safety stock, and a block-bootstrap scenario generator (block length 4 weeks, standardised errors) producing N demand paths around the test-origin forecasts. Check calibration of 80% and 95% intervals on the TEST year.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] results/forecast/error_sigma.csv has sku_id x horizon rows, all sigma > 0

- [ ] Test asserts that sigma uses only validation-window residuals
- [ ] Plot of 20 sample paths vs actuals for 1 SKU saved to results/figures/

Title: Plant simulator with age cohorts, FEFO and KPI accounting
Description: src/shelflife/sim/engine.py. Weekly loop given a production plan (quantity and sequence per week) and a demand path: add production as a new age-0 cohort; ship FEFO only units that satisfy minimum remaining shelf life; expire units older than shelf life (integer weeks); record lost sales on shortfall; compute changeover hours from the sequence (including carry-over from last week's final SKU) and flag capacity breaches. Output weekly KPI table per kpi_definitions.md.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] pytest invariant over 1000 random plans: produced = shipped + expired + ending inventory (+ initial inventory) for every SKU
- [ ] A hand-computed 3-SKU x 4-week example (committed as tests/fixtures/handcalc.md and .json) matches simulator output exactly
- [ ] Simulator is deterministic (same inputs -> identical KPI frame)
- [ ] KPI column names match docs/research/kpi_definitions.md
- [ ] 52-week x 12-SKU simulation runs in < 5 seconds

Title: Naive baseline planner (B1) with documented rationale
Description: Implement baseline B1, a realistic good-practice spreadsheet planner, NOT a strawman: forecast = 4-week moving average; weekly production = forecast demand + fixed 1-week cover top-up, scaled pro-rata if capacity is exceeded; sequence = fixed static 'allergen ladder' (fewest allergens first, most last, wet clean at end of cycle); FEFO. Document why this is fair and what it deliberately does not do (no shelf-life awareness, no dynamic sequencing).
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] docs/methods/baseline.md defines B1 rules numerically and gives a 'why this is not a strawman' paragraph
- [ ] Baseline plan is capacity-feasible for all 52 test weeks (checked by simulator flag)
- [ ] 52-week test replay runs in < 1 minute and writes results/baseline_replay.csv with all KPIs
- [ ] Baseline KPI values are plausible: expired waste > 0 and fill rate < 100% (else baseline is miscalibrated; recalibrate T2.2.2 or document)
- [ ] Unit test: with zero demand the baseline produces zero (no phantom production)

Title: Spike: choose MIP formulation (single model vs decomposition)
Description: TIME BOX 2.5h. Compare (A) one MIP with arc-based sequencing within each week (carry-over from prior week) against (B) decomposition: lot-sizing MIP with setup binaries and allergen-class setup estimates, then a CP-SAT circuit/TSP sequencing per week. Test on a 4-SKU x 8-week toy and a 12-SKU x 13-week instance. Also choose solver (OR-Tools SCIP / CP-SAT vs HiGHS). Record solve times and optimality gaps.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] notebooks/02_formulation_spike.ipynb contains both approaches on the toy instance with results table (solve time, gap, objective)
- [ ] docs/decisions/ADR-003-formulation.md states the choice, the evidence and the decision criterion: 12x13 instance reaches <=2% gap or a 120s time limit with a feasible incumbent
- [ ] Known limitations of the chosen approach (e.g. decomposition may be suboptimal) are listed
- [ ] Time box respected; if no approach hits the criterion, ADR records the fallback (decomposition + heuristic sequencing)

Title: Core lot-sizing MIP with age cohorts and shelf life
Description: src/shelflife/opt/model.py. Variables: production x[p,t], run indicator y[p,t], inventory by age cohort I[p,a,t], shipments, lost sales, expiry. Constraints: capacity (run hours + placeholder average changeover), min/max run size, cohort balance, ageing, minimum remaining shelf life at shipment. Soft demand satisfaction with lost-sales penalty. Objective weights from configs/costs.yaml (production, holding, expiry, lost sale, changeover). Document full math in docs/methods/optimization.md.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] docs/methods/optimization.md has sets, parameters, variables, objective and every constraint in math notation
- [ ] A 2-SKU x 4-week toy instance is solved by hand/brute force and matches the solver objective exactly (tests/test_model_toy.py)
- [ ] 12-SKU x 13-week model builds in < 10 s and solves with status logged (results/logs/)
- [ ] Infeasible/over-capacity input returns a clear status, not an exception (tested)
- [ ] LP file of the toy instance committed for inspection (tests/fixtures/toy.lp)

Title: Allergen-aware changeover and sequencing in the optimiser
Description: Add sequencing per ADR-003, including carry-over of the last SKU run in the previous week. Changeover hours come from the T2.2.2 matrix and consume capacity. The result must output an explicit run order per week.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Regression test: with all changeover times set to 0 the objective equals the T4.2.2 result
- [ ] Hand example where the allergen matrix forces a unique cheapest order; solver returns that order (test)
- [ ] Recomputed changeover hours from the output sequence equal the solver's changeover variable (assert on 5 instances)
- [ ] Output plan schema documented (week, line position, sku_id, qty, changeover_hours_before, clean_type)
- [ ] docs/methods/optimization.md updated with sequencing constraints

Title: Safety-stock constraints from forecast error
Description: Add soft lower bounds on projected end-of-week usable inventory: SS[p,t] = z(alpha) * sigma[p,h] (sigma from T3.3.1), with a shortfall variable and penalty, capped by what the shelf-life window allows. alpha is a parameter (default 95%, a TARGET service level assumption).
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Unit test: raising alpha from 0.80 to 0.99 raises mean safety stock monotonically
- [ ] SS cap by shelf-life window is implemented and tested on a slow-moving, short-shelf-life toy SKU
- [ ] Shortfall variable and penalty appear in docs/methods/optimization.md
- [ ] Model with SS builds and solves on the 12x13 instance within the time limit

Title: Rolling-horizon driver with logging and fallback
Description: src/shelflife/opt/rolling.py. Each week: take that origin's 13-week forecast, solve with a 60s limit, freeze week 1, advance the simulator with actual demand, carry inventory, log solve status/gap/time. If no feasible incumbent, fall back to the B1 plan for that week and count it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] 52-week test replay completes and writes results/optimized_replay.csv with the same KPI columns as the baseline
- [ ] results/logs/solves.csv has one row per week: status, gap, solve_seconds, fallback_used
- [ ] Number of fallback weeks is reported (target: 0; investigate if > 2)
- [ ] Every executed plan passes the independent checker (T4.3.3) - replay aborts otherwise
- [ ] Total replay runtime recorded (target < 90 min)

Title: Independent plan feasibility checker
Description: src/shelflife/checks/plan_checker.py re-validates any plan (baseline or optimised) against capacity, run-size limits, shelf-life/min-remaining rules and allergen/changeover accounting. It must not import the optimiser module, so it is an independent check.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Checker module has no import from shelflife.opt (verified by a test that scans imports)
- [ ] 5 mutation tests: deliberately corrupted plans (over capacity, below min run, wrong changeover accounting, expired shipment, missing clean) are all rejected with specific messages
- [ ] Baseline and optimised toy plans both pass
- [ ] CLI: `python -m shelflife.checks.plan_checker <plan.parquet>` prints PASS/FAIL list

Title: Experiment runner: historical replay and Monte Carlo
Description: scripts/run_experiment.py with a YAML config. Layer A: historical replay (real demand, real out-of-sample forecasts), baseline vs optimised, 52 weeks. Layer B: Monte Carlo with N demand paths (pilot to pick N; target 200) using common random numbers: baseline and optimised see identical paths. Save per-run KPI tables, config snapshot and git hash.
Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] `python scripts/run_experiment.py --config configs/experiment_main.yaml` runs from a clean state and writes results/experiments/<run_id>/{kpis.parquet,config.yaml,meta.json}

- [ ] Re-running with the same seed reproduces identical KPIs (hash comparison)
- [ ] Pilot (N=30) used to choose N so the bootstrap CI half-width on % waste reduction is <= 3 points (target); pilot output recorded
- [ ] Limitation recorded: in Monte Carlo layer, later-origin forecasts are not refit to simulated paths

Title: Statistical analysis and headline numbers
Description: src/shelflife/analysis/stats.py. For each KPI: paired differences, percentile-bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples) on mean difference and on relative reduction (1 - mean_opt/mean_base), Wilcoxon signed-rank as a secondary check, effect sizes. Write the single source of truth for resume numbers: results/headline_numbers.json.
Acceptance Criteria:

- [ ] Test on synthetic data with a known true effect: bootstrap CI covers the truth in >=90% of 100 trials

- [ ] A 'result is not what I hoped' section exists in docs/results/summary.md if any target is missed

Title: Sensitivity sweeps and waste-vs-service frontier
Description: Grid in configs/sensitivity.yaml, one-at-a-time: shelf life (-50/-25/0/+25%), changeover times (x0.5/1/1.5/2), forecast error scale (x0.5/1/1.5/2), utilisation (70/80/85/90/95%), minimum remaining shelf life (30/50/70%), cost weight ratios. Frontier: sweep baseline weeks-of-cover (0.5-3) and optimiser alpha (80-99%), plotting expired waste vs fill rate so that improvements are compared at matched service level. Use reduced N (e.g. 50) per cell and say so.
Acceptance Criteria:

Title: Sensitivity charts and honest robustness statement
